correctness.rationale: The complete claimed all-dimensional minimax is reconstructed from the exact Fock vacuum moment L=∫f dμ and averaged first-particle moment B=d^{-1}∫|z|² f dμ. These satisfy ||T_f-P_0||≥max(|1-L|,B). The Gamma(d+1)/Gamma(d) likelihood ratio is s/d; the single-threshold bathtub inequality at fixed L yields B≥M F_{d+1}(F_d^{-1}(L/M)), with equality forcing a radial ball among ALL measurable nonnegative symbols, not merely radial trials. The unique scalar crossing when M>1/2 is 1-MF_d(a)=MF_{d+1}(a); for M≤1/2, L=M requires f=M almost everywhere. The ball Toeplitz eigenvalues are exactly M F_{d+N}(a) for homogeneous degree N and decrease strictly, attaining this norm bound. Weyl displacement handles arbitrary center, and small-a Gamma expansion proves (d!)^{1/d}/(d+1) M^{-1/d}. Independently checked gamma-CDF balancing and ordered degree eigenvalues for five dimensions and eight budgets; these finite checks do not prove universal uniqueness.

The exact unique global optimizer, transition M=1/2, and dimension-dependent M^{-1/d} rate answer a meaningful approximation question; it is not a trivial restatement of radial diagonalization.
